review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for every use of closedUpperDisk and openUpperDisk in the lean tree. The uses are in HalfDiskGeometry, DiskBoundaryRegion, DiskTwoSideGlue, DiskSideRegionImages and DiskCrosscutHomeomorph. The file has no @[simp] lemmas and no membership characterisation for the two plain `def` sets. Downstream proofs unfold the definitions by name in `simp` calls. I did not check how the sibling definitions (diskDiameter, etc.) are simp-tagged. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour.

findings.problem: Both sets are plain `def`s with no canonical membership lemma such as `z ∈ openUpperDisk ↔ ‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im`, and no `@[simp]` on one. Every membership proof therefore has to unfold the definition by name. Within this file that happens at `simp [closedUpperDisk,mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right]`, `simp [openUpperDisk,mem_ball,dist_zero_right]` and `simp only [mem_sdiff,closedUpperDisk,openUpperDisk,mem_ofPred,mem_union]`. Downstream files do the same with `simpa [openUpperDisk,openLowerDisk] using hw` and `simp only [closedUpperDisk,closedLowerDisk,mem_inter_iff,mem_ofPred]`. The `mem_ofPred` rewrite exposes the set-builder representation, which is an internal detail. The clients cannot get the normal form `‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im` unless they list the definition names. If the definitions ever change, all of these call sites break.
findings.proposed_change: Right after the definitions, add `@[simp] lemma mem_closedUpperDisk {z : ℂ} : z ∈ closedUpperDisk ↔ ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ z.im := Iff.rfl` and `@[simp] lemma mem_openUpperDisk {z : ℂ} : z ∈ openUpperDisk ↔ ‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im := Iff.rfl`. Do the same for the lower-disk sets in DiskBoundaryRegion. The direction is safe: the right-hand side contains no occurrence of the defined constants, so it cannot loop. Then replace `simp [openUpperDisk,mem_ball,dist_zero_right]` with `simp [mem_ball,dist_zero_right]`, and likewise in `conj_image_openUpperDisk`, `closed_halfDisks_union` and `closed_halfDisks_inter`.
findings.benefit: One canonical, definitionally transparent membership normal form replaces repeated ad hoc unfolding lists in this file and in the DiskBoundaryRegion proofs. Proofs become shorter and no longer depend on how the sets are represented. Later `simp` calls get the half-disk membership unfolded without naming the constants.
